title: Feedback Speed
hook: I found out my offer wasn't working three months after launch. That's three months I can't get back.
statement: The faster you see results, the faster you improve. But only if you actually act on what you see.
explainer: Slow feedback means you keep doing the wrong thing for weeks. Fast feedback lets you course-correct while it's still cheap. Ignoring fast feedback is just as bad as not having it.
sop: List where you measure results and where you don't.
Rate the Speed of each feedback loop from 1 to 10.
Shorten the slowest loop. Check it weekly or daily, not monthly.
Rate your Adjustment from 1 to 10. Do you actually change things?
If Speed is high but Adjustment is low, fix the follow-through first.
equation_example: Speed 8, Adjustment 5. 8 × 5 = 40 out of 100. You're getting feedback fast but only half acting on it. Higher means quick feedback turns into real fixes. Lower means it's slow, or you're ignoring it.
question: Name one area where you're getting feedback too slowly to do anything about it.
closing_statement: Fast feedback you ignore is the same as no feedback.
caption:
Principle Nº 145: Feedback Speed
